raw_segments.text: If not the face of men, the sufferance of our souls, the time's abuse, if these be
motives weak, break off betimes, and every man hence to his idle bed.
So let high-sighted tyranny range on till each man drop by lottery.
But if these, as I am sure they do, bear fire enough to kindle cowards, and to steal with
valor the melting spirits of women, then, contramen, what need we any spur but our own
cause to prick us to redress?
What other bond than secret Romans, that have spoke the word, and will not paltor?
And what other oath than honesty to honesty and gagged, that this shall be, or we will
Swear priests and cowards, and men coddle us, old feeble carrions, and such suffering
Unto bad causes swear such creatures as men doubt, but do not stain the even virtue of
our enterprise, nor th, insuppressive metal of our spirits, to think that or our cause
or our performance did need an oath.
When every drop of blood that every Roman bears, and nobly bears, is guilty of a several
bastardy, if he do break the smallest particle of any promise that hath passed from him.
